title: Stone Game III
summary: Alice and Bob alternate, starting with Alice.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–50000 values in [−1000,1000]. A player must take at least one available stone on each turn.
contractDetails.output-checking: Exact typed equality of the returned str.

statement: Alice and Bob alternate, starting with Alice. Each turn removes one, two, or three remaining stones from the front and adds their signed values to that player’s score. Both play optimally. Return Alice, Bob, or Tie according to the final scores.

examples.explanation: Alice must take a negative score.
Taking the first three gives Alice 7 and leaves Bob 7.

constraints: 1–50000 values in [−1000,1000]. A player must take at least one available stone on each turn.
hints: Conceptual: Taking more now changes what the other player can take next.
Directional: Track the best score advantage from each starting position.
Implementation: For every legal take length, subtract the other player’s best suffix advantage from the value just taken. Keep the largest difference.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space using four rolling slots.
